title: Palace respects Ombudsman filing of plunder case vs Romualdez
summary: Malacañang said it respects the Office of the Ombudsman’s decision to file a plunder case against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, President Marcos’ cousin, over his alleged involvement in the…

blocks.text: Malacañang said it respects the Office of the Ombudsman’s decision to file a plunder case against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, President Marcos’ cousin, over his alleged involvement in the flood control scandal. In a press briefing on Monday, Sept. 7, Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said the Palace respects the Ombudsman’s decision as it is only performing its duties. “Iginagalang po natin ang aksyon ng Ombudsman dahil ito naman po ay nasa kanilang mandato (We respect the action of the Ombudsman because this is within its mandate),” she said. While the Palace had yet to receive a formal statement from President Marcos on the development, Castro said the President had already made clear his position on accountability. “Ang sa Pangulo naman po ay kung sino po ang dapat managot ay dapat na panagutin (The President’s position is that whoever should be held accountable should be held accountable),” she said. “Kung sino man po 'yan — kamag-anak, kaibigan, kaalyado, o kalaban sa pulitika (Whoever that may be — a relative, a friend, an ally, or a political opponent),” she added. Castro said the evidence should determine the course of the case, while those charged would have the opportunity to defend themselves. “Kung ano po ang isinisigaw ng ebidensya, dapat lamang po itong mailahad (Whatever the evidence shows, it should be brought to light),” she said. “Depende na po 'yan sa mga makakasuhan kung sila man po ay may sapat na ebidensya para ipaglaban ang kanilang sarili, nasa kanila na po 'yan (It will then be up to those charged, if they have sufficient evidence to defend themselves, to do so),” she added. Asked whether Marcos had expressed personal feelings about the case involving his cousin, Castro said she had not asked the President about it, but recalled his remarks during his fifth State of the Nation Address in July that he was prepared to let the evidence guide the government’s actions. “‘Pag ebidensya ang nagsusumigaw, kailangan po itong malaman ng taumbayan (When the evidence speaks, the people need to know about it),” she said. The Ombudsman filed the plunder case before the Sandiganbayan on Monday, accusing Romualdez and former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co of allegedly committing “concerted and coordinated acts” to unlawfully amass about P56 billion in ill-gotten wealth from 2022 to 2025. Romualdez has repeatedly denied involvement in the alleged flood control anomalies and has said he is ready to face the charges and prove his side, while his legal team has questioned the evidence against him. The filing follows Marcos’ July SONA disclosure that the Ombudsman was preparing criminal cases against his cousin. “Masakit man sa akin ito, pero kailangan nating gawin ang tama (Painful as this may be for me, but we have to do what is right),” the President said. “Hindi ako pangulo ng aking pamilya. Hindi ako pangulo ng aking kaibigan. Ako ay Pangulo ng Pilipinas at ang tungkulin ko ay sa inyo, ang aking mga kapwa Pilipino (I am not the president of my family. I am not the president of my friends. I am the President of the Philippines, and my duty is to you, my fellow Filipinos),” he added.
